Leo M.: hi team — new hire here. following k8s quickstart but `kubectl get ns` returns Forbidden after I switched to redwood-prod-norcal context. I only need dev-sandbox access for onboarding. any hints?

Onboarding Bot: Welcome Leo! Ensure you completed `redwoodctl login --sso` and then `redwoodctl sync-kubeconfig`. Docs: https://intranet.redwood/dev-onboarding#k8s. If you used multiple kubeconfigs, unioned KUBECONFIG can pick a file without creds.

Leo M.: I did SSO but I had KUBECONFIG set to `/home/leo/.kube/config:/home/leo/.kube/old-config`. output:
```
kubectl config current-context
# redwood-prod-norcal
kubectl get ns
# Error from server (Forbidden): namespaces is forbidden: User "system:anonymous" cannot list resource "namespaces" in API group "" at the cluster scope
```

Priya K.: hey leo — that anonymous error means kubectl isn't presenting your user token. Quick checks: `echo $KUBECONFIG`, `kubectl config view --minify --raw` (mask tokens). If you want to test without unsetting env, run `KUBECONFIG=/home/leo/.kube/config redwoodctl sync-kubeconfig --cluster=redwood-dev-west` then `kubectl config use-context redwood-dev-west`

Leo M.: ran the sync pointing to single file. `kubectl auth can-i get pods -n dev-sandbox` -> "no". I opened INFRA-9012 per the bot.

infra-bot: INFRA-9012 created: new-hire RBAC check for leom. Current: user is not in group "redwood:devs". Please confirm GitHub handle and org membership.

Leo M.: added GH handle. small Q: is the prod context expected in my kubeconfig during onboarding? I worry about accidental prod ops.

Priya K.: good question — we recommend you keep prod contexts in a separate kubeconfig file and not merge them during onboarding. docs say: "do not `kubectl` against prod from your workstation until you have completed prod training and have an additional approval." Also enable `kubectl config set-context --namespace=dev-sandbox` for safer defaults.

infra-bot: INFRA-9012 updated: rolebinding applied `namespace=dev-sandbox role=edit subject=group:redwood:devs`. Sync job completed.

Leo M.: ~20m later: `kubectl auth can-i get pods -n dev-sandbox` -> "yes" and `kubectl get pods -n dev-sandbox` lists pods. resolved, thanks! added note to onboarding doc about not merging prod kubeconfigs and testing `kubectl auth can-i` before running list/delete commands.

Priya K.: welcome aboard! I'll DM you a safe-commands cheat sheet and the link to our sandbox namespace dashboard. :tada:
